lines: behind the slowdown. However, excessively contractionary monetary policy has

lines: (y-o-y) in December 2023 to 12.4% in December 2024. This puts downward pressure

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, February 5 to 7, 2025
lines: in private capex in this sector. While demand expectations are important for

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, February 5 to 7, 2025
lines: investment decisions, the high interest rates have raised the risk premium assigned to

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, February 5 to 7, 2025

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, February 5 to 7, 2025
lines: in the flow of funds to the commercial sector. Total costs of bank/FIs-funded projects

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, February 5 to 7, 2025
lines: have seen no appreciable increase. The aggregate bank credit growth rate remains

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, February 5 to 7, 2025

lines: at 3.8 per cent and Q4 at 4.2 per cent; and FY: 2025-26 is at 4.2%. Undoubtedly, the

lines: 40.    Two inflationary risks have come to the fore since the February meeting. The first

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: risk emanates from the announcement of an output cut by OPEC+ during the weekend

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: just before the MPC meeting. Crude oil promptly reversed the entire price decline of the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: preceding weeks and settled slightly above the levels prevailing at the February meeting.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: The output cut by itself is not worrying as it could simply represent an attempt by OPEC+

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: to match supply to sluggish demand in a slowing global economy. It would become a

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: matter of concern only if it signals a structural change in the geopolitical alignment of the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: major oil producing countries. So far, the crude oil market has been relaxed about this

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: development with the futures curve continuing to slope downward. Nevertheless, the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: MPC needs to keep a careful watch on this evolving situation. If crude were to creep

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: towards the triple digit mark, there might be a need for a monetary response.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: 41.    The second risk relates to the monsoon. It is only around mid April that scientists

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: are able to provide monsoon forecasts with some degree of confidence, and the forecast

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: accuracy improves towards the end of May. In this meeting, therefore, the MPC has no

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: choice but to operate under the default assumption of a normal monsoon. However, in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: recent weeks, there has been increasing concern about some unfavourable

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: oceanographic patterns that could impact the monsoon this year. A deficient monsoon

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: would likely create inflationary pressures that would need to be counteracted with

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: monetary policy measures. We will however have to wait till May or even early June to

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: have reasonable clarity on this matter.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: 42.     On the growth front, early warning signs of a possible slowdown are visible to a

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: greater extent than in February. In the current situation of high inflation, monetary policy

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: does not have the luxury of responding to these growth headwinds. In fact, it is almost

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: axiomatic that monetary action can cool inflation only by suppressing demand. However,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: policy makers must be vigilant against overshooting the terminal policy rate, and thereby

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: slowing the economy to a greater extent than what is needed to glide inflation to the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: target.

lines: 43.    The balance of risks has, in my view, shifted slightly towards inflation since the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: February meeting, but the best estimate currently is that the 315 basis points of effective

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: tightening of the overnight interest rate (from a reverse repo rate of 3.35% to a repo rate

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: of 6.50%) would be quite sufficient to bring inflation under control. Therefore, I vote in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: favour of keeping the policy rate unchanged in this meeting.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: 44.    Turning to the stance, I must confess that I fail to comprehend its meaning. My

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: colleagues in the MPC assure me that the language is crystal clear to market participants

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: and others. It may well be that I am the only person who finds it hard to understand. But I

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: am unable to reconcile the language of the stance with the simple fact that no further

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: “withdrawal of accommodation” remains to be done since the repo rate has already been

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: raised to the 6.50% level prevailing at the beginning of the previous easing cycle in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: February 2019. It is of course possible to undertake further tightening, but that would not

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: constitute a “withdrawal of accommodation” by any stretch of the imagination.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: 45.    One interpretation that has been offered is that the real interest rate measured

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: using the most recent published inflation rate needs to rise further. This is doubtless true,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: but monetary policy should not be conducted by looking at the rear view mirror. The real

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: interest rate must be measured against the projected inflation rate 3-4 quarters ahead,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: and, as things stand right now, there is very little ground to argue for a further rise in the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: correctly measured real interest rate. Moreover, even if a flawed definition of the real

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: interest rate is accepted, the projected rise in this real rate would not require any action

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: by the MPC; it would happen as a mechanical result of a falling inflation rate and an

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: unchanged policy rate. And the projected fall in the inflation rate would be a consequence

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: of what the MPC has already done, and not what it will do in coming months.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: 46.      I cannot put my name to a stance that I do not even understand. At the same time,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: it is clear that the war against inflation has not yet been won, and it would be premature

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: to declare an end to this tightening cycle. There is need for heightened vigilance in the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: face of the fresh risks that I highlighted earlier in my statement. For these reasons, I

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: refrain from dissenting on this part of the resolution, and confine myself to expressing

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting, April 3, 5 and 6, 2023
lines: reservations on it.

lines: 20.     One of the pre-requisites of sustained economic recovery is the control over the pandemic.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 3-5, 2021

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 3-5, 2021

lines: faster than what was anticipated at the time of the October policy, although it must also be noted

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting December 2 to 4, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting December 2 to 4, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting December 2 to 4, 2020

lines: Urban demand is also showing signs of turning a corner. The Reserve Bank’s consumer confidence

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting December 2 to 4, 2020
lines: September. Optimism on early vaccine availability has also boosted economic sentiments.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting December 2 to 4, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting December 2 to 4, 2020
lines: capacity utilisation survey suggest that the capacity utilisation (CU) in the manufacturing sector is

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting December 2 to 4, 2020
lines: recovering, increasing to 61.7 per cent in Q2:2020-21 from 47.3 per cent in Q1:2020-21, although

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting December 2 to 4, 2020
lines: still lower than its long-term average. The expansion of the production-linked incentive (PLI)

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting December 2 to 4, 2020
lines: scheme to 10 more sectors is expected to boost manufacturing and exports.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting December 2 to 4, 2020
lines: policy rate actions has been sharper and quicker. Corporate bond yields have seen a significant

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting December 2 to 4, 2020
lines: reduction. Investment-related indicators such as imports and production of capital goods and

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting December 2 to 4, 2020
lines: consumption of steel and cement posted some sequential improvement in October. Corporate

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting December 2 to 4, 2020
lines: finances in Q2:2020-21 indicated some signs of recovery in demand conditions with profit margins

lines: rising due to savings in expenditure. Debt servicing capacity for manufacturing companies,

lines: measured by interest coverage ratio, improved in Q2:2020-21 with rise in profits. While

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting December 2 to 4, 2020
lines: profitability suggest that investment activity could rebound quickly as conditions normalise with

lines: Global Economy

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 6.      Incoming data point to a recovery in global economic activity in Q3 of 2020 in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: sequential terms, although downside risks have risen with the renewed surge in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: infections in many countries. Global trade is expected to be subdued. The rebound

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: could turn out to be stronger among advanced economies (AEs) than in emerging

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: market economies (EMEs). Global financial markets remain supported by highly

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: accommodative monetary and liquidity conditions. Soft fuel prices and weak

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: aggregate demand have kept inflation below target in AEs, although in some EMEs,

lines: Domestic Economy

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 7.      On the domestic front, high frequency indicators suggest that economic

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: decline in real GDP in Q1 (April-June). Cushioned by government spending and rural

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: demand, manufacturing – especially consumer non-durables – and some categories

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: of services, such as passenger vehicles and railway freight, have gradually recovered

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: in Q2. The outlook for agriculture is robust. With merchandise exports slowly catching

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: up to pre-COVID levels and some moderation in the pace of contraction of imports,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: the trade deficit widened marginally sequentially in Q2.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 8.     Headline CPI inflation increased to 6.7 per cent during July-August 2020 as

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020

lines: disruptions, higher margins and taxes. One year ahead inflation expectations of

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: households suggest some softening in inflation from three months ahead levels.

lines: Selling prices of firms remain muted, reflecting the weak demand conditions.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 9.     Domestic financial conditions have eased substantially, with systemic liquidity

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020

lines: Outlook

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 10.    Turning to the outlook for inflation, kharif sowing portends well for food prices.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: Pressures on prices of key vegetables like tomatoes, onions and potatoes should

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: also ebb by Q3 with kharif arrivals. On the other hand, prices of pulses and oilseeds

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: are likely to remain firm due to elevated import duties. International crude oil prices

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: have traded with a softening bias in September on a weak demand outlook, but

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: domestic pump prices may remain elevated in the absence of any roll back of taxes.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: Pricing power of firms remains weak in the face of subdued demand.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: COVID-19-related supply disruptions, including labour shortages and high

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: transportation costs, could continue to impose cost-push pressures, but these risks

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: are getting mitigated by progressive easing of lockdowns and removal of restrictions

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: on inter-state movements. Taking into consideration all these factors, CPI inflation is

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: projected at 6.8 per cent for Q2:2020-21, at 5.4-4.5 per cent for H2:2020-21 and

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 4.3 per cent for Q1:2021-22, with risks broadly balanced (Chart 1).

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 11.     Turning to the growth outlook, the recovery in the rural economy is expected to

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: strengthen further, while the turnaround in urban demand is likely to be lagged in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: view of social distancing norms and the elevated number of COVID-19 infections.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: While the contact-intensive services sector will take time to regain pre-COVID levels,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: manufacturing firms expect capacity utilisation to recover in Q3:2020-21 and activity

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: to gain some traction from Q4 onwards. Both private investment and exports are

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: likely to be subdued, especially as external demand is still anaemic. Taking into

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: consideration the above factors and the uncertain COVID-19 trajectory, real GDP

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: Q4. Real GDP growth for Q1:2021-22 is placed at 20.6 per cent (Chart 2).

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 12.    The MPC is of the view that revival of the economy from an unprecedented

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: COVID-19 pandemic assumes the highest priority in the conduct of monetary policy.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: While inflation has been above the tolerance band for several months, the MPC

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: judges that the underlying factors are essentially supply shocks which should

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: dissipate over the ensuing months as the economy unlocks, supply chains are

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: restored, and activity normalises. Accordingly, they can be looked through at this

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: juncture while setting the stance of monetary policy. Taking into account all these

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: factors, the MPC decides to maintain status quo on the policy rate in this meeting and

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: await the easing of inflationary pressures to use the space available for supporting

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: growth further.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 15.    Two key goals from the monetary policy perspective at the present juncture, in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: which output growth has declined sharply and inflation pressures remain, are

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: enabling sustained recovery of the economy and moderation in inflation rate.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 16.    The policy rates were left unchanged in the meeting of the MPC held on

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: August 4-6, 2020 after a cumulative reduction of 115 basis points in rates between

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: January and May 2020 in view of the prevailing modest GDP growth rate. The MPC

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: policy statement of August 2020 reflected the concerns on the economic outlook as

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: the COVID-19 pandemic began to take its toll.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 17.    The contraction in GDP in Q1: 2020-21, year-on-year basis, by 23.9 per cent,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: is a severe shock to the economy affecting employment and income. The decline in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: economic output is reflected in both production and expenditure accounts across

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: most components. The Gross Value Added declined in all the non-farm sectors and

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: in the case of demand, contraction in Private Final Consumption Expenditure and

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: Gross Fixed Capital Formation was sharp. The only major component of demand that

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: showed growth was Government Final Consumption Expenditure. Both exports and

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: imports of goods and services declined, with imports declining more than the decline

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: in exports. In the wake of COVID-19 pandemic, the extensive restrictions on the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: movement of goods and services barring the essential needs, imposed from the last

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: week of March-May saw gradual relaxation from June onwards but a full economic

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: recovery will require adjustments in the production and supply processes to control

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: the spread of the disease. The recovery process will also be affected by the dynamic

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: of the pandemic across the country as regional variations would also affect supply

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: chains.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 18.   The present status of the impact of the pandemic suggests that there has

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: been reduction in the daily new cases and mortalities due to COVID-19 towards the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: end of September but these numbers are large and the potential for an increase

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: cannot be ignored. This would mean that relaxation of movement restrictions would

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: help restore production, but the process would be gradual and subject to the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: measures that would be taken by the producers, providers of services and the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: consumers to control the spread of the virus.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 19.   Restoration of the supply side of the economy in a manner that is safe for the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: workers and the consumers is necessary for sustained economic recovery. There will

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: be a need for changes in transportation and work places to mitigate the risks

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: associated with the transmission of Covid 19.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 20.    The relative immunity of agriculture from the supply shocks may have been

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: partly a result of the fact that the virus spread initially in urban areas and there were

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: immediate efforts to limit the spread. The supply chains for the key food commodities

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: were also exempted from transport restrictions, leading to sustenance of supply of

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: these commodities.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 21.    There are indeed constraints that need to be addressed to restore the health

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: of the firms that have lost revenues and returns. Access to credit to revive and

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: expand production and markets is one of the essential factors in this regard. Bank

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: lending rates to the productive sectors including housing have declined and a robust

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: revival, however, would depend on the revival of demand. The weak demand

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: conditions are also reflected in the decline in non-food bank credit upto September in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 2020-21 over the previous year. Revival of consumer demand would require

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: restoration of confidence in the safety in participation in normal economic activities

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: and availability of health care. Public investment in improving infrastructure to

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: achieve these goals would help build consumer confidence.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 22.     The current account balance, foreign capital flows and forex reserves position

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: indicate relative stability in the external sector under a low demand equilibrium in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: both domestic and global markets. The depressed investment demand conditions are

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: also reflected in the dampened state of demand for capital and weak growth in bank

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: credit to non-food sector.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 23.     The fiscal position of the governments - both Centre and the States - is under

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: pressure as the tax revenues have declined. The governments will be required to

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: maintain their spending levels to meet the extraordinary demands to support

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: livelihoods and lives in the present conditions.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 24.     Continued weakness in demand conditions would put greater stress on fiscal

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: position and also the financial system.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 25.      The broad indicators of economic activity in the recent months suggest a

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: revival from the sharp decline in Q1. Some of this improvement is on account of

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: relaxation of movement restrictions, opportunities in sectors such as the pharma

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: industry, and the requirement of critical inputs such as fertilisers. The more general

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: pickup in activities is reflected in the expectation of improvement in capacity

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: utilisation and perceptions of improved demand conditions in the recent surveys of

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: enterprises reported by RBI.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 26.    The GDP will see sustained revival beginning from the second quarter of the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: year, with the rate of contraction from the levels of previous year declining steadily.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: As indicated in the MPC Resolution, the GDP growth is expected to be positive in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: Q4: 2020-21, although for the year as a whole, the growth rate is projected to be

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020

lines: conducted by RBI in September 2020 yields a median forecast of -9.1 per cent for the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: year 2020-21 and an assessment by NCAER’s Quarterly Review of the Economy

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: places the GDP growth for 2020-21 at -12.6 per cent. Going forward into Q2 to

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: Q4: 2020-21 these projections imply recovery in the economic activities from the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: large initial negative shock in Q1.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020

lines: which cannot be controlled in the short term except by removing bottlenecks in the

lines: supply chain upto the retail level or additional fresh supplies. As noted in MPC

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: drivers of price inflation on the supply side now are food and fuel. In the case of food,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: the favourable monsoon rains support the prospects of good harvest and its

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: moderating impact on food inflation. The global conditions for crude petroleum prices

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: appear stable from here onwards till the end of 2020-21.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 28.    There are clearly uncertainties facing the growth and inflation projections.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: There is also uncertainty over the speed with which the Covid-19 pandemic is

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: brought under control, which also affects growth and inflation scenarios in the next

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 2-3 quarters. Towards the end of Q2, there are indications of revival of the economy

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: after the relaxation of restrictions on transportation and businesses across the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: country. As supply chains adapt to the new conditions, recovery is expected to be

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: stronger and sustained. To achieve this outcome, an accommodative monetary policy

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: is needed at this juncture. Moderation in upward cost pressures on prices and decline

lines: in food inflation rates would require a quick output recovery from the supply side

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: measures.

lines: 29.    The outlook for growth and inflation for the next 3-4 quarters suggests the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: need for a policy environment enabling recovery of output. The inflationary pressures

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: are a concern but present assessment reflects moderating inflationary pressures in

lines: 56.    The projections of real GDP growth for 2020-21 that are set out for the first

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: time in the MPC’s resolution provide a sense of the wounds on the soul of the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: economy inflicted by COVID-19. If the NSO’s provisional estimates for Q2 that are

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: expected at the end of November corroborate at least the direction of these

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: forecasts, India has entered a technical recession in the first half of the year for the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: first time in its history. GDP is an aggregative indicator of economic activity and hides

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: the extent of human misery and the loss of social and human capital caused by the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: approximately 6 per cent below its pre-COVID level by the end of 2020-21 and it may

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: take years to regain this lost output. There is also an anecdotal sense that the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: economy’s potential output has fallen, and the post-COVID growth trajectory will look

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: very different from what has been recorded so far. Changes in social behaviour and

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: norms of commercial and workplace engagements may accentuate this structural

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: change.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 57.     Progressive unlocking of the economy has brought people out of isolation and

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: some high frequency indicators into the green. While this has raised optimism about

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: the much-awaited recovery, perhaps, pragmatic caution is warranted. The COVID

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: curve is arching inwards, from the cities where infections had hitherto festered, into

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: interior regions. The fear of a second wave looms over India; already it has forced

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: lockdowns across Europe, Israel and Indonesia, and India, with the second highest

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: caseload of infections and over-stretched healthcare infrastructure, cannot be

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: immune. In the absence of intrinsic drivers, the recovery may last only until pent-up

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: demand has been satiated and replenishment of inventories has been completed.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: Empirical evidence suggests that consumption-led recoveries are shallow and short-

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: lived. Exports could be a driver, but with the WTO’s latest projection of a decline in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: world trade volume by 9.2 per cent in 2020, the role of exports in powering a durable

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: revival is likely to be circumscribed. This underscores the critical role of investment in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: engineering the turnaround in the economy and sustaining it over the medium-term.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: Depressed capacity utilisation in manufacturing, inventory overhang in residential

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: housing, impaired balance sheets of corporates and financial institutions, and

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: pervasive business pessimism are combining to create formidable drags on

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: investment sentiment. Consequently, an investment-less recovery is doomed to be

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: ephemeral. Policy intervention accordingly assumes a vital role. Illustratively, public

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: investment can play both a gap-fill and crowding-in role. Monetary policy can

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: engender favourable financing conditions by lowering the cost of capital and by

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: narrowing risk spreads on financial instruments.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 58.     In the current milieu, however, both monetary policy and fiscal policy in India

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: face tightening constraints, some idiosyncratic. For fiscal policy, it is the collapse of

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: tax revenue – by 32 per cent in the first quarter; consequently, the centre’s revenue

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: deficit during April-August is 121.9 per cent of budget estimates. For monetary policy,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: it is the persistence of headline inflation above 6 per cent for the third month in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: succession. Structural reforms to unlock growth impulses are needed, but may lack

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: social traction in an atmosphere of depressed growth and employment, and high

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: uncertainty.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 59.     In the context of headline inflation ruling above the upper tolerance limit of the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: target since June 2020, the role of monetary policy has come under scrutiny. It has

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: been argued that while inflationary pressures may emerge from supply bottlenecks

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: and cost pushes, inflation cannot become generalised and persistent unless it

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: becomes a monetary phenomenon, i.e., it is accommodated by an increase in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: aggregate demand as reflected in an expansion of money supply or by a decrease in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: policy interest rates. Monetary policy has adopted an ultra-accommodative stance to

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: revive growth and mitigate the effects of COVID-19. Liquidity operations in support of

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: this stance have infused sizable liquidity into the system, reflected in reserve money

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: expansion of 17.6 per cent adjusted for the first-round effects of cash reserve ratio

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: changes. This has, however, not translated into a commensurate increase in money

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: supply because of a money multiplier depressed by a sharp increase in the currency-

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: deposit ratio, and remunerated reserves parked in reverse repo with the RBI over

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: and above CRR requirements. Consequently, the rate of money supply is averaging

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: 12 per cent in nominal terms and only 6 per cent in real terms. In terms of quarterly

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: seasonally adjusted annualised rates, a negative money gap has opened up recently.

lines: 61.     Under these conditions, it is essential for monetary policy to remain

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: accommodative and opportunistically exploit the headroom that opens up when

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: inflation recedes, as it is projected in the second half of 2020-21. Three aspects need

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: to be emphasised. First, it is important to separate false starts from durable growth

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: drivers. In this context, all efforts need to be trained on the revival of investment.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: Second, in the evolving situation in which monetary policy is committed to an

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: of generalization and persistence. For this purpose, all indicators of aggregate

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020
lines: demand, including monetary and credit aggregates, warrant continuous examination

lines: for inflation impulses. Third, with unprecedented contractions in economic activity and

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting October 7 to 9, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 25.     Since the last review, the economy has seen a gradual rebound in economic activity.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: This is largely mechanical, as much of the lockdown in the economy is being undone as

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: policy constraints on the supply side are removed.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 26.     Average CPI headline inflation has been above the target range’s upper bound (6 per

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: cent) for the last 6 months (6.7 per cent between January – March 2020, 6.5 per cent between

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: April-June 2020). While the NSO’s imputed estimates for April-May 2020 inflation require

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: more clarity, it is clear that just looking at CPI headline inflation in March 2020 (5.8 per cent)

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: and June (6.1 per cent) means that the trend is upwards. Inflation excluding food and fuel (i.e.,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: core inflation) also rose to 5.4 per cent in June. Higher price momentum in most sub-groups

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: of core inflation saw some increase in May and June suggesting that core inflation remains

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: high and sticky.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 27.     On the other hand, after the April peak, food price momentum has subsided, which has

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: largely been driven by the decline in cumulative momentum in vegetables. This however

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: needs to be carefully watched. Both 3-month and 1-year ahead inflationary expectations

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: increased marginally by 10 basis points to 10.4 per cent and 10.5 per cent respectively. The

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: “levelling-off” of inflationary expectations from a steady increase since March 2020 is

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: comforting.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 28.     The prospect of an “inflation whipsaw”, a phrase used by Markus Brunnermeir at

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: Princeton, is probably the right way to look at inflation going forward, i.e., there are different

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: inflation/deflation pressures that need to be watched carefully. On the upside, a perfect storm

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: of cost push pressures, accommodative monetary policy, and adverse food supply shocks

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: could lead to a pickup in inflation. On the downside, the paradox of thrift, i.e., forced saving

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: pressure induced by a “de-facto” lock-down, could be a potent disinflationary force.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 29.    In terms of output losses, my assessment is that the worst is almost surely behind us

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: (notwithstanding second waves of the pandemic etc.).

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 30.   Economic crosscurrents however make it difficult to diagnose precisely the underlying

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: damage because of the virus over the next year.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 31.     Real GDP growth in Q4 FY 20 based on provisional estimates produced by the NSO is

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: now pegged at 3.1 per cent. This is the weakest print in the new data series that started in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 2012-2013. The complete year FY20 real GDP growth is 4.2 per cent, which is also the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: weakest in the series. Netting out government expenditure’s contribution in Q4 FY20, private

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: demand growth remains anaemic. Consumption growth, for instance, in FY 20 was 5.3 per

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: cent compared to 7.2 per cent in FY 18-19 and 8.1 per cent in FY 16-17. In FY 21, these

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: numbers will be compounded by idiosyncratic shocks to particular sectors because of Covid

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: (aviation, tourism) where the policy response has not been adequate.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 32.     Credit growth continues to remain muted despite large rate cuts. I worry that a

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: negative credit supply shock to the MSME sector may lead to a “credit-gap”, i.e., a reduction

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: in the supply of credit to small firms, leading to small businesses to shift towards higher cost

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: providers of credit. This will have a bearing on growth. Some of these issues have begun to be

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: addressed in amendments to the recently announced ECLGS scheme by the government. I

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: worry though that if credit continues to be expensive, these firms will become less capital

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: intensive over time, leading to a lower marginal product of labour. The long run equilibrium

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: for the economy will involve a negative impact on wages, and therefore demand.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 33.      Some high frequency indicators however have begun to turn in June. To name a few,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), PMI services, PMI manufacturing, electricity output,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: some rural demand indicators like tractor sales, and GST collections have retreated from their

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: earlier lows in April-May. A tentative global recovery is also happening. The distribution of

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: rainfall has overall been positive. Monetary transmission has also improved. This is crucial

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: given the close connection between sovereign yields and funding conditions in the economy.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: For instance, between March-July 2020, the policy repo rate was cut by 115 bps. The WALR

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: for fresh rupee loans during this period declined by 91 bps. Despite this I worry though that

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: given that there is a lot of uncertainty on the investment side, the option value of waiting will

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: be big, which will delay the onset of investment spending.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 34.    There are other risks due to Covid that pose downside risks to growth in the medium

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: run.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 35.    For instance, Covid is simultaneously a negative demand and a negative supply shock.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: Macro policy broadly must ensure that a temporary Covid type shock to the Indian economy

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: does not become permanent. Economists call this hysteresis. In a post-Covid world, as Olivier

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: Blanchard notes, hysteresis will be driven by human behaviour. Despite the economy opening

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: up, people will still hesitate to go out and spend. This will limit the effects of unlocking the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: economy.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 36.     I continue to maintain that the major brunt of future fiscal stimuli should be tilted

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: towards social insurance payments and on the taxation side, where the multipliers are larger.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: It is important to recognize that fiscal multipliers depend on country characteristics. They are

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: smaller in countries with flexible exchange rate regimes, open to trade, and with high levels of

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: public debt. India has all three. Fiscal multipliers may be larger at the zero lower bound, but

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: India is not there yet. Prices are also more flexible in developing countries like India because

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: of the presence of a large informal sector. This weakens the transmission of fiscal policy from

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: financial markets to the real economy. Fiscal stimulus design will have to keep these factors

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: in mind, and will have a strong bearing on the type of cyclical recovery that the economy

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: experiences. Economic policy is a potent tool for equilibrium selection at the current juncture.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 37.   This should be a crisis that is not wasted. The government must continue to focus on

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: much needed structural reforms. Some fiscal space should be reserved for later outbreaks.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 38.     Given the above reasons, it would be opportune to wait and watch to see how the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: growth-inflation numbers pan out over the next few months. I therefore vote to pause. I also

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: vote to retain the stance as accommodative.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 39.     I should mention that I have been advocating a more cautious path for policy rate

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: reductions since February 2019. However, I have been in a minority in the MPC. Inflation

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: has now been above the upper band of 6 per cent for a number of months. Notwithstanding

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: large rate cuts to spur growth over the last year and a half, growth has steadily declined

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: despite 250 bps in cuts since February 2019. Future MPCs should not go soft on inflation.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: Going forward, monetary (and fiscal) policy will be needed to be used wisely with a clear

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: understanding of what and what not they can achieve in terms of controlling inflation,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: smoothening out the business cycle, and limiting spurious economic volatility.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 40.    I have been contributing to the setting of monetary policy since February 2013 (first

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: on the TAC, and now on the MPC). I want to thank the Reserve Bank of India and the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting August 4 to 6, 2020
lines: Government of India for giving me this opportunity.
