lines: 47.     In recent weeks, there has been a drastic change in the global and domestic

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: macroeconomic scenarios. Coronavirus (COVID-19) has crippled global supply chains

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: and disrupted economic activity in many countries. The outbreak of coronavirus initially

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: began as a supply shock, but it soon also became a demand shock with restrictions on

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: travel, tourism, and cut back in non-essential spending due to lockdowns. Reflecting the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: severe impact that the COVID-19 is expected to have on the global economy, financial

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: markets have been witnessing turbulence.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: 48.     The authorities in many countries, including central banks, have unleashed

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: conventional and unconventional measures to mitigate the adverse macroeconomic

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: impact of the pandemic. Despite massive easing by central banks, however, global

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: financing conditions have tightened due to a flight to safety. That there has been so much

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: flight for safety and demand for liquidity that there has been large selling even in gold,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: pulling down its prices, which normally rise in an uncertain environment.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: 49.    Since the pandemic is still spreading and its impact deepening, the estimates for

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: downward drag on global growth are continuously being revised. However, it is now clear

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: that global growth in 2020 is likely to be much weaker than that in 2019. As the COVID-

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: 19 pandemic has impacted advanced and emerging economies alike due to lockdowns

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: and impaired supply chains, there is, in fact, a serious risk that the global economy will

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: even slip into recession in 2020. In the face of slowing down of global growth, huge global

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: debt accumulated after the global financial crisis may also pose serious threats to global

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: financial stability.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: 50.     Moving on to the domestic economy, economic activity appeared to have picked

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: up some pace as reflected in several indicators in January/February such as growth in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: IIP, including manufacturing; railways freight traffic; tractor sales; and credit to micro and

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: small industries. Both exports and imports also turned positive in February. PMI

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: manufacturing in January and PMI composite in February were at eight-year high.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: However, these past data have become less relevant as the near-term outlook has turned

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: highly uncertain caused by COVID-19, the spread, strength and length of which are

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: unknown at this stage.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: 51.    Various segments of the financial market have become extremely volatile and

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: trading volumes have declined, pushing yields across the spectrum of yield curve. The

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: domestic equity market has plummeted in the face of massive sell-offs by foreign portfolio

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: investors. On the whole, domestic financial conditions have tightened and could seriously

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: undermine monetary transmission, which otherwise improved in the more recent period.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: 52.     While initially it was the civil aviation, hospitality and entertainment sectors which

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: were hit by COVID-19, now with a 21-day nation-wide lockdown, most sectors will take a

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: hit in Q4: 2019-20 and Q1:2020-21. The number of infected cases is relatively still low in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: India. And with the nation-wide lockdown if the spread is contained, life could slowly start

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: returning to normalcy and the economy could also start recovering gradually. However,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: growth for the year as a whole is likely to be weak for three reasons. First, discretionary

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: spending by households is likely to be curtailed in general even though there could be

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: some pent-up demand in some sectors. Second, external demand will remain weak,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: impacting our exports. Third, weak domestic and external demand is likely to cause a

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: delay in revival of investment activity. However, the increased government spending may

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: cushion the slowdown.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: fall in global LPG prices. CPI inflation ex food and fuel is expected to remain soft on

lines: account of two factors: (i) a slowdown in demand; and (ii) a sharp decline in international

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: also on input prices in many industries. However, the decline in domestic pump and LPG

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: prices will occur only to the extent the pass-through takes place. On the whole, the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020

lines: during the period of lockdown would be challenging, which may, therefore, hamper a

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: clearer assessment of the price situation for immediate months.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: 54.     On the whole, it has been hard to clearly assess the macroeconomic outlook at

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: this point of time. The COVID-19 pandemic has led to a series of a priori indistinguishable

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: shocks – a sharp slowdown in global demand, volatility in financial markets, a sharp fall

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: assigning probabilities on outcomes in times of infrequent but high-impact events such as

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: the COVID-19 pandemic for projection purposes is extremely daunting.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: 55.     To sum up, there is an unprecedented uncertainty about the exact impact COVID-

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: 19 will have on the near-term growth outlook. Though difficult to quantify, it is clear that

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: aggregate demand will weaken significantly in the near future, which will impact the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: have been under stress with yields hardening across the maturity spectrum, do not

lines: normalising, domestic demand would need to be stimulated without any loss of time. The

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: inflation outlook has improved significantly. Keeping in view these considerations, the

lines: need of the hour is to effect a sizeable reduction in the policy rate. I, therefore, vote for

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: with several other liquidity enhancing measures being separately announced by the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: Reserve Bank should ease financing conditions and address financial stability risks. I also

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: vote for persevering with the accommodative stance as long as necessary to revive

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: growth and to mitigate the adverse impact of COVID-19, while ensuring that inflation

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting March 24, 26 and 27, 2020
lines: remains within the target.

lines: upwards towards headline CPI inflation as it did in the period prior to that suggesting

lines: 36.    Headline CPI inflation in December spiked to 7.35% from 5.5% in November,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: and 4.6% in October. The sharp uptick in headline inflation was driven by a sharp

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020

lines: 37.    While some of the increase in the October–December 2019 food inflation

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: (average 9.3%) relative to October–December 2018 inflation (average -1.2%) was

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: so far has tracked the average momentum between 2012-13 and 2016-2017 much

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020

lines: y-o-y in December), it would be prudent to remain watchful of the outsized shocks to

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: food.

lines: in November and 3.4% in October reflecting higher increases in telecom tariffs (which

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 39.    In a testament to the success of flexible inflation targeting in India - helped

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: NSO. The first advance estimate (FAE) for 2019-2020 puts Private Consumption

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: weak.

lines: 41.    Real sales of 286 listed private manufacturing companies in the manufacturing

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: sector in Q3: 2019-2020 continued to weaken. Capacity utilization was lower at

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 42.     On the prospects for investment, what is disconcerting is that despite the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: enactment of the September 2019 corporate tax cut, there is no discernible increase

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: in net profits in Q3:2019-20 across several firm types in RBI’s Industrial Outlook

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: Survey (IOS). Profit margin expectations for Q4 also continue to be pessimistic

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: across firm types. While it may still be early, the “impact effect” of the corporate tax

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: cut appears to have been to accelerate the extent of corporate deleveraging rather

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: than increase planned capex in an environment with weak demand. The impact of

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: the corporate tax rate on investment, capital deepening, and wage growth will

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: cut.

lines: 43.    On the positive side, broader economic activity is beginning to show

lines: 44.    Eight core industries grew in December (1.3 %) and the full IIP grew in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: November (+1.8%) after four and three consecutive months of contraction,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: respectively. Several high frequency indicators have turned and/or strengthened

lines: since the last review: PMI Services, PMI Manufacturing, the Manufacturing IIP,

lines: Consumer Non-Durables, High Rabi sowing, Vehicle registration, Rail freight, GST

lines: Tax collections, and Cement and Steel Production amongst others. Monetary

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 45.     The government had an unenviable position of walking a fiscal tightrope in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: Budget 2020. I see the corporate tax cuts and the personal income tax rationalization

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: in this budget as part of the same combined stimulus. Taking the budget estimates

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: at face value, a rough calculation suggests that this amounts to a tax-stimulus of

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: about 0.9% of GDP (26 USD Billion / 2.9 USD Trillion). The stimulus (in the form of

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: reductions in various rates) from the GST since its implementation in July 2017

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: probably amounts to an additional 0.3 % of GDP. The combined tax stimulus

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: therefore approximates 1.2 percentage of GDP given the initiatives in the 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: budget.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 46.  If growth hasn’t revived with a 135 bps cut in the policy rate, and a tax stimulus

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: amounting to 1.2% of GDP, then the need of the hour is more structural reform.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: tighter than desired monetary conditions to ensure our commitment to the medium-

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: term inflation target.

lines: 48.   Real GDP growth during March 2015 – September 2019, has averaged 7.2%.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: This would suggest that the Indian economy has performed like a “7-4” economy

Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: (averaging roughly 7% growth and roughly 4% inflation) over the period of flexible

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: inflation targeting. I find the growing chorus challenging the efficacy of flexible

lines: inflation targeting in India worrying. For those who advocate targeting an inflation rate

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: higher than 4 per cent, I am sorry: 4-6% inflation is not price stability!

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 49.    In sum, monetary policy continues to be well positioned. While I don’t see

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: space for further cuts going forward, I remain data dependent. While the current

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: spike in headline inflation is likely to lack persistence, the inflation numbers should be

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: carefully watched.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 50.  Given the above reasons, I vote to pause. I also vote to retain the stance as

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020

lines: 51.    Headline inflation, measured by CPI inflation, increased to 7.4% in December

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 2019 (highest since July 2014) from 5.5% in November and 4.6% in October,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: primarily due to a sharp rise in food inflation to 12.2% in December. This, in turn, was

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: mainly due to an increase in onion prices, accompanied by a rise in inflation in milk,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: pulses, cereals, edible oils, eggs, meat and fish. At the same time, CPI inflation

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: excluding food and fuel rose to 3.8% in December from 3.4% in October, driven

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: primarily by an increase in inflation in the transport and communications sub-group.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 52.     Going forward, both survey data and model-based forecasts indicate a

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: moderation in inflation. According to RBI’s Inflation Expectations Survey of

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: Households, conducted in January 2020, inflation expectations eased by 60 and 70

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: basis points over three-month and one-year ahead horizons, respectively, possibly

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: due to an expected moderation in food prices. As per the December 2019 round of

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: RBI’s Industrial Outlook Survey, manufacturing firms expect subdued selling prices in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: Q4:2019-20 as input costs are also expected to remain muted. Further, projections

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: made by RBI indicate that inflation is expected to moderate but remain at elevated

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: levels (5% or above) through Q2:2020-21.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 53.     The future inflation trajectory is subject to various factors, including downside

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: risks such as sharper than expected moderation in onion prices and larger correction

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: in prices of other vegetables due to higher production. Upside risks include an

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: increase in global food prices, rise in gold prices, fluctuations in oil prices due to geo-

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: political tensions, and an increase in input costs for services. Disruptions in the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: supply of Chinese imports due to the spread of coronavirus may also exert pressure

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: on prices of goods imported from China.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 54.   On the output front, industrial production grew by 1.8% y-o-y in November, a

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: sharp turnaround from -4.0% in October. Growth in broad categories under the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: sectoral classification as well as the use-based classification either increased from

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: the previous month or the extent of contraction eased (with the exception of

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: intermediate goods that grew by double-digits though the pace moderated). Growth

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: turned from negative to positive for the mining and manufacturing sectors, whereas

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: the contraction in growth eased in electricity. The pace of contraction also eased for

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: primary goods, capital goods, infrastructure and construction goods, and consumer

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: durables, while it turned from negative to positive for consumer non- durables.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 55.    According to the first advance estimates released by the National Statistical

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: Office (NSO), real GDP growth for 2019-20 is pegged at 5%, while GVA growth is

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: estimated at 4.9%. The estimates indicate a deceleration in consumption and

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: investment as well as a contraction in exports, with reduced demand for imports.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: Industrial growth is also expected to decline, while agricultural growth is expected to

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: edge up – as rabi sowing has been higher than the previous year.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 56.     Turning to survey data, RBI’s Order Books, Inventory and Capacity Utilisation

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: Survey (OBICUS) shows a drop in capacity utilisation in the manufacturing sector in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: Q2:2019-20 compared to Q1. The Business Assessment Index (a composite of

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: demand indicator), based on the RBI’s Industrial Outlook Survey for the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: manufacturing sector, remained in the contractionary zone for Q3:2019-20. At the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: same time, the Business Expectations Index shows prospects of improvement for

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: Q4. According to RBI’s Consumer Confidence Survey, the Current Situation Index fell

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: to a new low in January 2020 due to weaker sentiment on general economic

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: situation, price level and household income. On the other hand, the Future

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: Expectations Index witnessed a marginal uptick due to improved outlook on

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: employment and prices. Meanwhile, the Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: increased from 51.2 in November to 55.3 in January 2020, reflecting an increase in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: new orders and output. The PMI Services Index also picked up during this period. A

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: few high frequency indicators are also showing signs of revival, such as tractor sales,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: three-wheeler sales, railway freight traffic and domestic air passenger traffic.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 57.     Thus, there are some signs of a modest revival, although overall economic

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: activity continues to remain weak. While the focus of the Union Budget is on

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: sustainable growth within a framework of fiscal consolidation, it may provide some

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: impetus to growth through the incremental rationalisation in personal taxes, focus on

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: infrastructure and rural spending, emphasis on raising competitiveness in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: manufacturing and enhancing the overall ease of doing business. However, the full

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: impact of these measures may percolate slowly to the economy with possibly only a

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: small effect visible in the short-run.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 58.     Flow of credit to the commercial sector, that remained tepid till the MPC met

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: last in December, picked up in the last two months. This should nurture growth

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: impulses. The increase in the monetary transmission of the cumulative reduction in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: the policy repo rate by 135 basis points from February to October 2019 should also

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: help in reviving economic activity. The weighted average lending rate (WALR) on

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: fresh rupee loans sanctioned by banks fell by 69 basis points from February to

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: December 2019 (implying an additional 25 basis points in November and December).

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: Since the introduction of the external benchmarking system, many banks have linked

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: their lending rates for housing, personal and micro and small enterprises (MSEs) to

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: the policy repo rate. From October to December 2019, the WALRs of public and

lines: private sector banks on fresh rupee loans fell by 18, 87 and 23 basis points for

lines: housing loans, vehicle loans, and loans to MSMEs, respectively. Thus, the external

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: benchmarking system has improved the extent of transmission, although there is still

lines: scope for more.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: 59.    Moving on to the international front, some signs of a cyclical upturn in global

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: industrial growth are in sight. On the verge of the coronavirus outbreak, growth in the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: Economic Cycle Research Institute’s (ECRI’s) 21-Country Long Leading Index, a

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: harbinger of global economic activity, entered a mild cyclical upturn consistent with

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: global industrial growth had already begun, following a modest upturn in the growth

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: rate of ECRI’s Global Leading Manufacturing Index. In that context, it is notable that

lines: the coronavirus epidemic is not yet tipping global industrial growth into a fresh

lines: cyclical downturn. However, this has to be monitored closely to gauge the possible

lines: 60.    Aligned with the improvement in global growth prospects, growth in ECRI’s

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020
lines: Indian Leading Exports Index, a predictor of Indian exports growth, has increased

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020

lines: recently, anticipating a revival in Indian exports growth, which has dropped to a multi-

lines: can get a boost from global growth.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 4 to 6, 2020

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019
lines: 24.     In the fifth bi-monthly monetary policy resolution in December 2018, CPI inflation for

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019
lines: 25.     Several factors will shape the inflation path, going forward. First, food inflation has

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019
lines: months. Electricity prices also showed an unexpected moderation, providing a softer outlook for

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019
lines: the fuel group. Thirdly, while inflation excluding food and fuel remains elevated, the recent

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019
lines: unusual pick-up in the prices of health and education could be a one-off phenomenon. Fourthly,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019
lines: the crude oil price outlook remains broadly the same as in the December policy. Fifthly, the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019
lines: Reserve Bank’s surveys show that inflation expectations of households as well as input and

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019
lines: output price expectations of producers have moderated significantly. Finally, the effect of the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019
lines: HRA increase for central government employees has dissipated completely along expected lines.

lines: Taking into consideration these developments and assuming a normal monsoon in 2019, the path

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019
lines: H1:2019-20 and 3.9 per cent in Q3:2019-20, with risks broadly balanced around the central

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019
lines: trajectory.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019
lines: Looking beyond the current year, the growth outlook is likely to be influenced by the following

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 5-7, 2019
lines: Q3 – with risks evenly balanced.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

lines: of accommodation. This is in spite of the softening of inflation in recent prints. Let me explain

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: in some detail.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: 54.       An inflation targeting central bank needs to separate “signal” from “noise” in the data:

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: •   Recent prints have softened due primarily to easing of vegetable prices (contributing to

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: not suggest that this is due to durable supply management in vegetables. Instead,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: reasonable conclusion is that vegetable prices continue to show seasonality over years,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: albeit with some variation in months in which the seasonality kicks in. This volatility is

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: largely “noise” from an interest-rate setting perspective; this volatility is also not

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: something amenable to monetary policy actions, and certainly not at short horizon of a

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: few months at which it is likely to, and typically does, revert.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: •   What concerns me is that the more persistent component of headline inflation, which is

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: ex food and fuel, and which one can consider as the “signal” given its persistence, has

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: strengthened steadily from a trough of 3.8 per cent last June to 4.4 per cent in February

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: over this period, and also confirmed by input price pressures and selling price increases

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: •   The inflation trajectory over the entire twelve-month period is projected, despite the soft

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: •   Professional forecasters surveyed by the Reserve Bank also expect the inflation to stay

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: over 4 per cent for much of 2018-19.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: •   While there is inevitable uncertainty around these inflation projections, I view the risks as

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: tilted significantly to the upside given the continuing rise in the ex-food-and-fuel

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: inflation. Besides oil prices, my another primary concern is the risk of fiscal slippages,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: at both the Centre and State levels, especially in the form of:

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: o   A shift away from capital expenditures towards revenue expenditures, as is

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: already being seen in state expenditure to accommodate farm loan waivers; and,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: clearly induce an upside bias to potential inflation risks (estimates vary widely

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: from 10 basis points to close to 100 basis points depending on what measures are

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: adopted).

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: •   Finally, as the Indian economy is economically as well as financially integrated with the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: also pose a major challenge to the external sector.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

lines: 56.     CPI inflation moderated in January-February, led largely by a sharp decline in vegetable

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

lines: 58.     Economic activity has been recovering, with the GDP growth in 2018-19 projected to be

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018
lines: There are clearer signs of revival of investment activity. The manufacturing sector is

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting April 4-5, 2018

lines: (crude and products) due largely to high international prices. Gold imports increased – both

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: Outlook

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 19.     The December bi-monthly resolution projected inflation in the range of 4.3-4.7 per

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: cent in the second half of 2017-18, including the impact of increase in HRA. In terms of

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: actual outcomes, headline inflation averaged 4.6 per cent in Q3, driven primarily by an

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: unusual pick-up in food prices in November. Though prices eased in December, the winter

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: seasonal food price moderation was less than usual. Domestic pump prices of petrol and

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: diesel rose sharply in January, reflecting lagged pass-through of the past increases in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: international crude oil prices. Considering these factors, inflation is now estimated at 5.1 per

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: cent in Q4, including the HRA impact.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 20.      The inflation outlook beyond the current year is likely to be shaped by several factors.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: First, international crude oil prices have firmed up sharply since August 2017, driven by both

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: demand and supply side factors. Second, non-oil industrial raw material prices have also

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: witnessed a global uptick. Firms polled in the Reserve Bank’s IOS expect input prices to

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: harden in Q4. In a scenario of improving economic activity, rising input costs are likely to be

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: passed on to consumers. Third, the inflation outlook will depend on the monsoon, which is

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: assumed to be normal. Taking these factors into consideration, CPI inflation for 2018-19 is

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: estimated in the range of 5.1-5.6 per cent in H1, including diminishing statistical HRA impact

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: of central government employees, and 4.5-4.6 per cent in H2, with risks tilted to the upside

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: (Chart 1). The projected moderation in inflation in the second half is on account of strong

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: favourable base effects, including unwinding of the 7th CPC’s HRA impact, and a softer food

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: inflation forecast, given the assumption of normal monsoon and effective supply

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: management by the Government.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 21.     Turning to the growth outlook, GVA growth for 2017-18 is projected at 6.6 per cent.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: Beyond the current year, the growth outlook will be influenced by several factors. First, GST

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: implementation is stabilising, which augurs well for economic activity. Second, there are

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: early signs of revival in investment activity as reflected in improving credit offtake, large

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: resource mobilisation from the primary capital market, and improving capital goods

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: production and imports. Third, the process of recapitalisation of public sector banks has got

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: underway. Large distressed borrowers are being referenced for resolution under the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC). This should improve credit flows further and create

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: demand for fresh investment. Fourth, although export growth is expected to improve further

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: on account of improving global demand, elevated commodity prices, especially of oil, may

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: act as a drag on aggregate demand. Taking into consideration the above factors, GVA

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: growth for 2018-19 is projected at 7.2 per cent overall – in the range of 7.3-7.4 per cent in H1

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: and 7.1-7.2 per cent in H2 – with risks evenly balanced (Chart 2).

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 22.      The MPC notes that the inflation outlook is clouded by several uncertainties on the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: upside. First, the staggered impact of HRA increases by various state governments may

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: push up headline inflation further over the baseline in 2018-19, and potentially induce

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: second-round effects. Second, a pick-up in global growth may exert further pressure on

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: crude oil and commodity prices with implications for domestic inflation. Third, the Union

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: Budget 2018-19 has proposed revised guidelines for arriving at the minimum support prices

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: (MSPs) for kharif crops, although the exact magnitude of its impact on inflation cannot be

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: fully assessed at this stage. Fourth, the Union Budget has also proposed an increase

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: in customs duty on a number of items. Fifth, fiscal slippage as indicated in the Union Budget

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: could impinge on the inflation outlook. Apart from the direct impact on inflation, fiscal

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: slippage has broader macro-financial implications, notably on economy-wide costs of

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: borrowing which have already started to rise. This may feed into inflation. Sixth, the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: confluence of domestic fiscal developments and normalisation of monetary policy by major

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: advanced economies could further adversely impact financing conditions and undermine the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: confidence of external investors. There is, therefore, need for vigilance around the evolving

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: inflation scenario in the coming months.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 23.      There are also mitigating factors. First, capacity utilisation remains subdued. Second,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: oil prices have moved both ways in the recent period and can potentially soften from current

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: levels based on production response. Third, rural real wage growth is moderate.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 24.    Accordingly, the MPC decided to keep the policy repo rate on hold and continue with

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: the neutral stance. The MPC reiterates its commitment to keep headline inflation close to 4

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: per cent on a durable basis.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 25.     The MPC notes that the economy is on a recovery path, including early signs of a

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: revival of investment activity. Global demand is improving, which should help strengthen

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: domestic investment activity. The focus of the Union Budget on the rural and infrastructure

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: sectors is also a welcome development as it would support rural incomes and investment,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: and in turn provide a further push to aggregate demand and economic activity. On the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: downside, the deterioration in public finances risks crowding out of private financing and

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: investment. The Committee is of the view that the nascent recovery needs to be carefully

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: nurtured and growth put on a sustainably higher path through conducive and stable macro-

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: financial management.

lines: Statement by Dr. Chetan Ghate

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 28.      Since the last review, there has been a sharp increase in headline inflation

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: (November, 4.9%; December, 5.2%). The latest reading is, worryingly, led by rising inflation

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: in all major groups. Both food and fuel inflation have also increased, with the usual seasonal

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: easing in food inflation getting delayed till December. Global demand – with world GDP

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: projected to grow at approximately 3.9% in 2018 – could push oil prices higher. All measures

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: of inflation have converged above 5%. Adverse supply side shocks could push the Phillips

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: curve of the economy upward posing a strong risk to the medium-term inflation target of 4%.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 29.     Inflation, excluding food and fuel (December, 5.2%) is up although this is primarily

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: due to the statistical boost from Centre’s HRA. Pricing decisions by firms may possibly be

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: responding more to the recent increases in input costs, driven by a reversal of the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: international commodity cycle, rather than staff costs, driven by a tightening of the labour

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: market, or higher capacity utilisation. This suggests that inflation excluding food and fuel may

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: be increasing more because of cost-push factors, which will worsen the growth-inflation

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: trade-off.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 30.     There are fewer mitigating factors to rising inflation compared to two months ago.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: Rural wage growth continues to be moderate but with an uptick, possibly reflecting a rise in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: construction activity. The deflation in pulses continues but could reverse with the new

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: procurement policy announced in the Union Budget of 2018-2019. At the current juncture

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: though, stripped of cereals and vegetables (volatile items), the increase in inflation net of

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: volatile items, from its trough in June 2017, is less pronounced. Both 3-month and 1-year

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: ahead inflationary expectations are also stable.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 31.     In my last review, I had flagged how increases in MSP by the government could lead

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: to generalized inflation, and worsen monetary transmission, based on research (with co-

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: authors). While details on the exact procurement policy are awaited, the enactment of a more

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: elaborate procurement policy in the 2018-2019 Union Budget will put stress on state finances

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: as well. Fiscal slippages in India are inflationary!

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 32.    With respect to economic growth, data trends have largely been positive in the last

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: few months, as suggested by many high frequency indicators. My main concern in the last

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: few reviews was whether animal spirits in the economy will sustain GDP growth beyond the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: base effect induced increases in Q3 and Q4 2017-2018. This looks increasingly likely.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 33.      Profit margins in the manufacturing sector are improving, with sales being higher in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: real terms. The PMI in services increased in December and January. The RBI enterprise

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: surveys also suggest a substantial improvement in demand conditions. Several high

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: frequency activity indicators have picked up suggesting that the growth deceleration has

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: troughed. The flow of financial resources by banks and non-banks is also picking up. It is

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: highly possible however that current growth trends will make the economy accelerate into an

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: inflationary phase. This needs to be watched with laser-like precision.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 34.     Ultimately, any durable increase in growth in GDP however will depend on investment

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: demand. The figure below, using the KLEMS database, plots growth in output per worker

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: against growth in capital stock per worker between 1980 and 2011. While the figure is merely

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: suggestive, it does indicate that output per worker has tracked capital per worker fairly

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: closely during this period, suggesting dynamics in output per worker in India in the medium

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: term are described reasonably well by a Solow-Swan style model. Any durable increase in

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: output per worker will only come about by increases in capital per worker. To that extent, the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: recent uptick in investment/GDP ratio is encouraging.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 35.    Taking these considerations into account, I vote for a pause in the policy repo rate at

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: today’s meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: be passed on to the consumers and lead to higher CPI inflation. Households’ inflation

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018

lines: 38.     At the same time, positive signs of economic growth are visible. To begin with, the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018

lines: 45.     In April last year, I expressed a preference for a pre-emptive policy rate increase,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: sensing that inflation is rising out of the demonetisation trough. I voted, however, for holding

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: the rate unchanged through the June and August meetings to allow transitory effects to fully

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: pass. My vote for status quo was maintained in August even though the Committee by

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: majority decision reduced the policy rate by 25 basis points in that meeting.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 46.      By the October meeting, my stance had been vindicated. Looking ahead, I saw

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: inflation stripped of house rent allowance effects exceeding the target by the end of the year.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: Worrying that a vicious spiral could be developing – input costs; domestic prices of petroleum

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: products; inflation expectations – as the slowdown in growth troughed and geared to pick up

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: in the second half of the year, I provided specific forward guidance.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: readiness to raise the policy rate if inflation drivers strengthen. By the December meeting,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: upward adjustments of domestic POL prices in response to the hardening of international

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: crude prices, including catching up with withheld pass-through; imminent MSP increases;

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: fiscal slippage; customs duty increases. Various measures of underlying inflation are

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: converging to the headline at above 5 per cent. Expectations are elevated and volatile. Fixed

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: income markets are telling us that we have fallen behind the curve.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 49.     In the near term outlook (up to mid-2018), inflation is likely to drift well above target. It

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: is important to recognise that the expected easing of inflation in the outer months of the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: forecast horizon – between July 2018 and March 2019 – is largely statistical as the HRA

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: effect wanes. The target is in danger of getting out of reach and over the next few months,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: the upper tolerance band is under threat. This could seriously dent the credibility of the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: Committee’s commitment to the target.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 50.     Turning to the state of the economy, a turnaround has likely begun in the third quarter

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: of 2017-18 – sales are accelerating even as inventories are being drawn down; the capex

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: cycle is starting up; and pricing power is returning. External demand is providing support as

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: exports grow at ASEAN rates. Accelerating growth in non oil non bullion imports is reflecting

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: domestic demand, including substitution effects, impatient with the sluggishness in the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: supply response.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 51.    The output gap is starting to turn up from a persistently negative state. If the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: professional forecasters’ consensus around 7 per cent plus growth for 2018-19 materialises,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: the output gap is expected to close going forward.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: below 1 per cent and could fall further absent policy action. This is completely misaligned

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: with underlying fundamentals and the economy's prospects at a time when activity is picking

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: up. In view of the prolonged period of status quo, a series of rate increases may be

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: warranted to remove excessive accommodation. The time to begin is upon us.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 53.    I vote for an increase of 25 basis points in the policy rate to commence the withdrawal

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: of accommodation.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: Statement by Dr. Viral V. Acharya

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 54.     Headline inflation prints since last policy have been significantly above the target.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: While a part of this is statistical due to the Centre's HRA implementation, there has also been

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: a rise in inflation sans HRA. A major concern has been the steep rise in oil prices

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: coincidentally with (i) global rates and commodity cycles having turned up; and (ii) our fiscal

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: deficit having overshot for this year and likely to do so next year too. Hence, even without

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: factoring in the States’ staggered HRA implementation and MSP rises announced in the

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: Union Budget, risks to inflation seem clearly tilted on the upside. Indeed, RBI's projections at

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 12-14 months in future put headline inflation by more than 50 basis points above the target

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: (by then the statistical effect of Centre’s HRA implementation would have completely waned).

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 55.     Such an inflation scenario would imply a raise in policy rates by a pure inflation-

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: targeting central bank, in turn, implying a change in stance from "neutral" to "withdrawal of

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: accommodation." However, two reasons induced me to pause.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 56.      First, an important factor determining inflation going forward is likely to be the shale

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: gas production response to rising oil prices; while this response has been somewhat muted,

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: its trigger out of dormancy could dampen oil prices swiftly. I would like to see whether this

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: downside risk plays out in next few months to have a firmer grip on the medium-term inflation

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: trajectory.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 57.    Second, for a flexible inflation targeting framework, the growth trajectory relative to

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: potential output has to be considered too.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 58.     On this front, the output gap remains somewhat negative though it has been steadily

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: closing. Structurally, the improving balance sheets of the banking system post

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: recapitalisation package and the ongoing resolution of large stressed accounts have made

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: the recent pick up in credit growth more sustainable. Real economic activity indicators also

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: suggest a broad-based growth revival. While RBI growth projections for next year are in line

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: with this buoyant activity of late, the recovery is nevertheless nascent and worthy of some

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: support in the short run.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: 59.      Given these trade-offs, I vote for a pause with no change in the neutral stance. The

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: next few months of inflation and growth data will be key to determining the evolution of policy

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: rates. If growth remains robust and inflation prints continue to project headline inflation a year

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: ahead well above the target, then a change in stance from "neutral" to "withdrawal of

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: accommodation" might have to be considered.

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: undertaken in improving the transmission of policy rate changes to the real sector; and (ii)

identifier: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting February 6-7, 2018
lines: taking the resolution framework for stressed assets to its logical conclusion.
